title: This Frog Hides 89% of Its Blood to Turn Invisible While Asleep

scenes.text: This frog turns see-through when it sleeps.
Glass frogs have clear skin, but their red blood still gives them away.
So when they sleep, they hide it. Up to 89 percent of their red blood cells move into the liver.
Sleeping frogs end up as much as 61 percent more see-through.
A predator scanning the leaf sees no frog.
It's still there. You just can't see it.

description:
This frog turns see-through when it sleeps.
A 2022 study in Science found that sleeping glass frogs pack up to 89 percent of their red blood cells into the liver, making them up to 61 percent more transparent. Researchers say how the cells pack without clotting could help human medicine.
Could you spot a sleeping glass frog? Comment below.
first_comment: The blood goes to the liver without clotting. Scientists want to know how. Any guesses?
